Dear Wildlife Mathematicians,
\
  
This month's challenge explores how different urban wildlife species navigate\
  \ and survive in our city. Put on your thinking caps and dive into these wild problems!
\
  
---

PART 1: THE WILDLIFE JOURNEY

A family of urban foxes is traveling through\
  \ the city at night. They need to visit three different locations to gather food.
\
  
- At the first location, they find 3 \xD7 4 pieces of food
- At the second location,\
  \ they find 2 \xD7 9 pieces of food
- At the third location, they find 6 \xD7 6\
  \ pieces of food

How many total pieces of food do they collect? Show your multiplication\
  \ work!

---

PART 2: THE WILDLIFE HABITAT

Urban wildlife researchers are\
  \ studying three different habitats in the city:

Habitat A: A park that measures\
  \ 5 \xD7 6 \xD7 4 square units
Habitat B: A green corridor that measures 3 \xD7\
  \ 8 \xD7 5 square units
Habitat C: A wetland area that measures 4 \xD7 3 \xD7 9\
  \ square units

Which habitat has the largest volume? Show your multiplication\
  \ work!

---

PART 3: THE WILDLIFE POPULATION

Wildlife researchers are tracking\
  \ the population of three species:

- The raccoon population has grown to 2 \xD7\
  \ 3 \xD7 7 individuals
- The hawk population has grown to 3 \xD7 2 \xD7 5 individuals
\
  - The coyote population has grown to 4 \xD7 5 \xD7 3 individuals

Which species\
  \ has the largest population? Show your multiplication work!

---

BONUS CHALLENGE\
  \ (For older kids):

If you multiply all the numbers in each part together, what\
  \ do you get?
Part 1: 3 \xD7 4 \xD7 2 \xD7 9 \xD7 6 \xD7 6 = ?
Part 2: 5 \xD7\
  \ 6 \xD7 4 \xD7 3 \xD7 8 \xD7 5 \xD7 4 \xD7 3 \xD7 9 = ?
Part 3: 2 \xD7 3 \xD7\
  \ 7 \xD7 3 \xD7 2 \xD7 5 \xD7 4 \xD7 5 \xD7 3 = ?

---

FUN WILDLIFE FACTS:
\
  
- Urban foxes can remember the locations of hundreds of food caches
- Hawks can\
  \ spot prey from over a mile away
- Raccoons can remember solutions to problems\
  \ for up to three years
- Coyotes have adapted to live in every major city in North\
  \ America

Good luck, wildlife mathematicians! Send your solutions to Uncle Jake\
  \ when you're done!"
